text:
sam: CI image-scan failed on build #4921 at 2026-03-18T09:02Z — secret detector flagged "artifact/signature.pem" and decrypt step errored: KMS AccessDenied for service-account:ci-builder@redwood. Pipeline is blocked. Anyone seen this before?

dev-bot: deploy-bot posted scan result -> https://go/reports/ci/4921 (scan id 2026-03-18-09-02).

lee: Is this the same regression after the RBAC cleanup we did on Friday? @security-oncall

mia: Looks like the key policy no longer includes the CI SA after the role flattening. Two approaches: re-add SA to key ACL (fast, risky) or grant Decrypt via ephemeral IAM role assumed by CI using workload identity (preferred).

security-oncall: Recommend ephemeral role + full audit. Short plan: (1) temporary allow to unblock CI, (2) capture audit evidence, (3) open ticket for permanent workload-identity solution and key rotation. Who can apply the temporary grant?

sam: I can do a 1-hour temporary binding to unblock and then revoke. Will annotate the audit entry and attach logs.

lee: Paste the minimal IAM binding you plan to add so we can review before you apply.

sam: ```json
{
  "bindings": [
    {
      "role": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter",
      "members": ["serviceAccount:ci-builder@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],
      "condition": null
    }
  ]
}
```

ops-bot: policy change submitted by sam (change-id: 9876). Applied to key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/deploy/cryptoKeys/sign-key. Audit entry created: https://audit.redwood/internal/entries/9876

mia: Quick note: the scanner flagged the key file inside the image, not a repo secret. We should add evidence in the suppression request: build logs, image manifest, and path `/opt/build/keys/signature.pem`. That will speed up triage.

security-oncall: Agreed. Please attach the following to the ticket: (1) build log snippet showing decrypt error, (2) full image manifest, (3) confirmation that the file is generated at build time and not checked into source. We'll treat this as a false-positive for SAST but need to harden the IAM flow.

sam: Attaching logs in the ticket now. Link: https://go/tickets/4523. Short mitigation implemented and CI unblocked.

lee: For the permanent fix I propose: use CMEK with a dedicated key, workload identity for CI runners, and rotate the key after we migrate. Also add a signed-image verification step so unsigned images fail early.

security-oncall: I'll create an action item to update the SAST/DAST config to exclude build-time artifact paths (prefix `/opt/build/`). Also will add this scenario to the oncall runbook: if CI shows KMS AccessDenied -> check IAM binding -> temporary allow (owner: sam) -> capture audit id -> escalate to sec-eng if >3 occurrences in 24h.

mia: Can ops confirm we have `kms.decrypt` logs routed to the SIEM index so we can search by audit id? @ops-bot

ops-bot: Confirmed. `kms.decrypt` events for key `projects/redwood-prod/keys/sign-key` at 2026-03-18T09:02:31Z (attempts: 3). SIEM link: https://siem.redwood/search?q=entry:9876

sam: I'll file the PR for workload identity + update the CI runner config. PR will include a test job that simulates decrypt with short-lived creds. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

security-oncall: Thanks — adding permanent owner: @lee for the key-migration task. Closing this thread once PR merges and a follow-up ticket for key rotation is created. :white_check_mark:

sam: Closing — PR link will go into ticket #4523 when ready.
